## 2. Detail

### R-01 · Tiered client size budget

**Context.** RNF-01 caps the embeddable script at 45 KB gzipped; CA-03 extends this to a Lighthouse claim (≤2-point drop). Engineering estimates put a complete client (widget + capture + editor + i18n + masking) at 35–55 KB gzipped in a single bundle — sitting exactly on the line. Two components dominate: the annotation editor (10–16 KB hand-rolled) and DOM-serializing capture (8–14 KB). `fabric.js` is ≈85 KB gzipped and `html2canvas` ≈50 KB gzipped — each would blow the budget alone.

**Decision.**

| Tier | Limit (gzipped) | Enforcement |
|------|-----------------|-------------|
| `watchbug.js` — injected core, capture + masking + widget | **≤ 45 KB**, hard | `npm run check:size`, fails CI |
| Any lazy companion chunk (annotator, optional adapters) | ≤ 25 KB each | same script |
| Total client payload at runtime | ≤ 80 KB | same script |

**Rationale.** The invariant's *intent* is "cost the host page nothing" (RNF-01: async, non-blocking). A tiered budget keeps the hard 45 KB line on the thing that is actually injected while acknowledging the editor is fetched on user gesture and never on the critical path. Raising the number later becomes a one-line change to one tier, not a constitutional rewrite.

**Consequence.** The annotation editor **must** be a lazy chunk. Capture and masking must be dependency-free or near it.

---

### R-02 · Pragmatic hexagonal architecture

**Decision.** Ports and adapters at exactly these eight seams. Plain modules everywhere else — no interface ceremony.

| Port | Default adapter | Notes |
|------|-----------------|-------|
| `CaptureSource` | `DisplayMediaCapture` | Produces a bitmap of current app state |
| `Redactor` | SEC-01 rule pipeline | Hosts may register additional rules |
| `Enricher` | URL / UA / viewport / console | Hosts may register additional providers |
| `Annotator` | own canvas editor | Lazy chunk (R-01) |
| `Transport` | `fetch` + `keepalive` | |
| `Storage` | filesystem volume (R-04) | S3/MinIO is a reserved second adapter |
| `AuthProvider` | single-admin env (R-05) | Static bearer token is a reserved second adapter |
| `WidgetHost` | closed Shadow DOM (R-14) | |

**Rationale.** Six of the open consultation items were open precisely because they were being treated as irreversible architecture. Under this map each becomes "which adapter ships by default", which is cheap to revisit. It also satisfies the owner's stated goal of *"a modular architecture with some plugs where you can connect extra features to expand in the future"* without over-engineering a TFG codebase.

**Declare the No.** Reserved ports are **seams only**. No adapter will be built for Jira / GitHub / Slack / Trello, session replay, or AI triage — those remain `mission-brief.md` §2 non-goals. The seam is free; the work is out of scope.

---

### R-03 · Deliverable scope

Code only in this repository and in this GSD roadmap. The academic *memoria* and any user-facing documentation site are separate tracks. Keeps roadmap phases shippable-software-shaped.

### R-04 · Attachment storage — filesystem volume

Screenshots and other blobs live on a named volume / bind mount. Metadata lives in PostgreSQL.

**Hard requirement:** blobs are served **only** through the authenticated API, never as static files — otherwise the volume is a path-traversal vulnerability.

**Rejected:**
- *Postgres `bytea`* — atomic and one-`pg_dump` backup, but bloats `pg` and degrades it at scale. Documented fallback if ops simplicity ever outweighs scale.
- *S3 / MinIO* — production-grade and pre-signable, but adds a **4th** container, extra `.env` secrets (SEC-04 surface), and a harder demo. It is the reserved second `Storage` adapter.

**Rationale.** INV-03 names exactly three services in `docker-compose.yml`: API, static panel, persistent DB. A filesystem volume keeps that promise literally true.

### R-05 · Panel auth — single admin from `.env`

`WATCHBUG_ADMIN_USER` / `WATCHBUG_ADMIN_PASSWORD` read from `.env`, hashed with **Argon2id** (bcrypt acceptable fallback) at boot. Login issues a JWT with a defined TTL in an `HttpOnly` / `SameSite=Lax` / `Secure` cookie. Satisfies SEC-06 in full.

**Rejected:** multi-user accounts (pulls in signup, email verification, password reset, an SMTP service — none appear in RF-01…08); static bearer token only (no logout, no TTL, and it lives in `localStorage`, against SEC-06).

Password change = edit `.env` + restart. Acceptable for single-team self-hosting; a static-token `AuthProvider` adapter is reserved for CI/automation use.

### R-06 · Multiple projects per deployment

`projects(id, name, public_key, created_at)`. Incidents FK to project. Panel exposes a project selector.

**Explicitly v2:** per-project settings, members, roles, quotas, key rotation UI.

**Note on scope.** `mission-brief.md` §2 excludes *"multi-tenancy SaaS gestionado por nosotros"* — that is a **hosting model** exclusion. Multiple projects inside one self-hosted install is not excluded.

### R-07 · Apache-2.0

Permissive **plus an explicit patent grant**, which matters given the canvas-masking and capture technique. `NOTICE` attribution required.

**Hard constraint applied:** the SDK is `<script>`-embedded into third-party commercial web apps. A viral license on the client bundle would make the tool unusable in practice. AGPL-3.0 was rejected on exactly this ground despite its ideological fit with "self-hosted". MIT rejected for lacking a patent grant. MPL-2.0 rejected as unusual for this space.

⚠ **Open dependency (Q-05):** confirm the degree-awarding institution's IP policy before the repository is made public.

### R-08 · URL is path-only

`environment.url` carries scheme-origin + path. Query string and fragment are discarded at the SDK, before they ever leave the browser.

**Rationale.** Query strings routinely carry `?token=`, `?code=`, `?session=`. Stripping is a blunt, total mitigation; a denylist is a partial one with an unbounded failure mode. Hosts needing more add a custom `Enricher`.

### R-09 · End-user identity — on by default, opt-out

```jsonc
"user": { "id": "u_123", "name": "Ana", "email": "ana@example.com" }
```

**Bound interpretation (technical necessity, not preference).** SEC-03 forbids the SDK from reading host cookies, `localStorage`, or auth headers. The SDK therefore **cannot** discover who the end user is. The only implementable reading of "on by default" is: the host passes `user` into `Watchbug.init({...})`, and it rides along on every report unless `privacy: { userIdentity: false }`. If the host supplies nothing, nothing is sent.

⚠ This makes the panel a store of personal data → RGPD Art. 13 notice duty and Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation apply. See R-10.

### R-10 · Retention

Identity fields (`user.*`) auto-purged after N days, default **30**, configurable in `.env`. The report itself is kept, anonymised. The admin can at any time delete a report entirely or erase its identity fields immediately.

**Rejected:** manual delete only (relies on a human remembering); whole-report auto-delete (loses history for no privacy gain once identity is gone).

### R-11 · WebP with PNG fallback

WebP at q≈0.8, PNG where unsupported. 1920×1080 screenshot: WebP ≈60–150 KB vs PNG ≈300–800 KB — a ~5× difference in storage and bandwidth. Masking runs on `ImageData` **before** encode (SEC-02) so the choice is orthogonal to privacy.

### R-12 · E2E / property verification only

**Owner directive, stated twice: "DONT MAKE A BUNCH OF TESTS. Only make e2e as necessary, not unit tests."** This is policy.

| Kept | `npm run check:size` — RNF-01/CA-03 build gate |
|---|---|
| **Kept** | **One** Playwright e2e suite, 5 groups mapping 1:1 to CA-01…CA-05. Target ≈20 assertions. |
| **Abolished** | `test:unit` entirely — no formatter tests, no i18n-formatter tests, no per-function tests, no coverage thresholds. |

**Collision resolved.** CA-02's stated verification is *"test unitario del componente de canvas"* — the only one of CA-01…05 that names a unit test. Resolution: **change the verification method, not the property.**

- Old method: unit-test `manipularMatrizPixeles()` → proves a function mutates an array.
- New method: e2e drives the real widget, applies a mask, **intercepts the outgoing HTTP request**, decodes the attached image, and asserts the masked region's original pixel values are **absent from the encoded bytes**.

The new method proves SEC-02's *"irreversible"* at the artifact that actually leaves the browser. Strictly stronger evidence for less code.

**Consequence.** `mentorship-pack.md` §3.1 is derogated; §3.2 is folded into the same suite as contract assertions; §3.3 is retained but scoped to CA; §3.4 is retained.

### R-13 · Masking must not be reconstructible

Derived from SEC-02 + CA-02 while resolving R-12.

Gaussian blur is **linear and invertible in part** — a motivated attacker can deconvolve a blurred region and recover structure. Therefore the mask **must** be one of:

- solid fill (absolutely irreversible), or
- block-averaged pixelation with **block size ≥ 8 px** (irreversible at pixel level).

Gaussian blur is prohibited. `filter: blur()` CSS overlays were already prohibited by SEC-02.

### R-14 · Shadow DOM isolation ◆ Proposed

Production bundle: `mode: 'closed'`. A build-time flag (`SHADOW_MODE=open`) emits an e2e-only bundle so Playwright can pierce the root and assert on i18n strings and form state under hostile CSS (CA-04).

**Why not runtime-configurable:** it widens the public SDK interface (`mission-brief.md` §3 restricted decision) for no production benefit. A build flag gives CA-04 full assertability at zero runtime cost. INV-01 permits `'open'` or `'closed'`; `closed` is the stronger reading.

### R-15 · TypeScript end-to-end ◆ Proposed

| Workspace | Contents |
|---|---|
| `packages/contracts` | **The** official payload schema (Zod) + exported TS types + JSON Schema emit. Single source of truth for CA-01. |
| `packages/sdk` | Client. TypeScript, near-zero runtime deps, esbuild → IIFE + ESM. |
| `apps/api` | Fastify 5 + `@fastify/rate-limit` (SEC-05) + `@fastify/cors` + `@fastify/multipart` + Drizzle ORM + `pg`. |
| `apps/panel` | React + Vite + TS. Static SPA (INV-03). Not size-constrained. |
| — | PostgreSQL 16. Three compose services: `db`, `api`, `panel`. |

**Rationale.** CA-01 says *"el esquema JSON oficial"* — singular. Every two-language split (Pydantic + TS types, Go structs + TS types) creates two sources of truth for the one invariant that exists to prevent drift. `packages/contracts` imported by SDK, API and panel makes drift structurally impossible. Secondary: `npm run test:*` / `check:size` become literally native; one toolchain and one Docker base image serve the *"lo más generalistas para el usuario"* goal.

**Rejected:** Python/FastAPI + TS SDK (schema duplication + two toolchains + two base images); Go + TS SDK (same); PHP/Laravel + TS SDK (SDK is TS regardless, so the win is partial).

Fastify's plugin ecosystem is itself the "plugs" mechanism the owner asked for at the HTTP edge, complementing R-02's ports in the domain core.

⚠ **Exact versions (Node, Fastify, Drizzle, Postgres, React) are NOT fixed here.** They must be verified against live documentation during the RESEARCH step — training-data version numbers are not evidence.

### R-16 · `AGENTS.md` is non-authoritative

Owner statement: *"Whatever decision is in AGENTS.md is not final and I did not make them, it was a previous file I forgot to delete."* Only `mission-brief.md`, `mentorship-pack.md` and `ase-instructions.md` govern. `AGENTS.md` will be regenerated by the GSD workflow as `$INSTRUCTION_FILE` and will then describe the real project.

### R-17 · No calendar-driven descoping

*"The submission horizon is when it's finished completely and well done with good quality."* Scope is therefore cut by **coherence**, never by deadline pressure. Every quality gate in the Mentorship Pack remains hard. v1 is the smallest *complete and defensible* set; v2 items are deferred because they belong to a later slice, not because time ran out. The roadmapper plans for depth over breadth.

## 3. Dead-ends

Approaches evaluated and rejected. Do not re-explore.

| ID | Dead end | Why |
|----|----------|-----|
| D-01 | Treating `AGENTS.md` as a governing document | Stale scaffolding from a previous setup (R-16). |
| D-02 | Reading `npm run test:*` vs `pytest` as a contradiction | False. The Mentorship Pack's commands cover *client-side* concerns only; `pytest` covered the backend. Disjoint layers, both correct. |
| D-03 | Reading RNF-01's 45 KB as a single whole-project budget | Replaced by R-01's tiered budget. |
| D-04 | `html2canvas` for capture | ≈50 KB gzipped — larger than the entire client budget. |
| D-05 | `fabric.js` / `konva` for the annotator | ≈85 KB and ≈45 KB gzipped. Editor must be hand-rolled (R-01). |
| D-06 | Gaussian blur as the masking primitive | Partially invertible by deconvolution — fails SEC-02's "irreversible" (R-13). |
| D-07 | Python 3.10 as backend target | End-of-life October 2026. Moot under R-15, recorded so the number does not reappear. |
| D-08 | `html-to-image` / SVG `foreignObject` DOM serialization as the primary capture path | ~8–14 KB and silently fails on cross-origin images, `<video>`, WebGL, fonts and host closed shadow roots. Retained only as an optional `CaptureSource` adapter. |
